topics.label: Lecture introduction and objectives
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic introduces the lecturer, the cancer lecture series, and the core learning objectives concerning environmental carcinogens and cancer development.

topics.label: Mutational and evolutionary basis of cancer
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics establish cancer as a genetic and microevolutionary disease driven by endogenous DNA damage, replication errors, and inherited predispositions within a permissive microenvironment.

topics.label: Environmental carcinogens, public risk perception, and epidemiology
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine recognized environmental exposures, public interpretation of the bad luck hypothesis, and epidemiological data demonstrating geographical and migrant variations in cancer incidence.

topics.label: Infectious agents and viral oncogenesis
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics detail how microbial and viral pathogens induce cancer, using Burkitt lymphoma as a multi-factorial case study of viral oncogenesis.

topics.label: Chemical and physical mutagens and xenobiotic metabolism
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine how dietary toxins, UV radiation, and chemical carcinogens induce DNA damage directly or through endogenous xenobiotic metabolic activation.

topics.label: Tumor promotion, host tissue susceptibility, and mechanistic summary
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explore how non-mutagenic drivers, such as chemical promoters and developmental proliferative states, cooperate with DNA damage to facilitate tumor outgrowth.

topics.label: Methodologies for identifying and testing carcinogenicity
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics outline the genomic signatures, epidemiological cohort studies, animal models, and in vitro assays used to identify carcinogen exposure and evaluate carcinogenic potential.

topics.label: Carcinogenic risk assessment and lecture conclusion
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic concludes the lecture by framing carcinogenic exposure in the context of everyday risk-benefit decisions and summarizing the primary lecture themes.
